m11_f3_status_ignored.what: zeros_checked ignores cudaMemset's returned status (order K5)
m11_f3_status_ignored.order_source: K5: it can fail only if a fill can be made to fail; if no test can see it, record it as unkillable by test, with the reason
m11_f3_status_ignored.reason: The mutant differs from F3 only when cudaMemset returns a non-success status on the fill of an allocation the helper has just made. A non-sticky error from an earlier call is not returned by a later, successful cudaMemset (the CUDA runtime reports it through the last-error slot, which neither F3 nor the mutant reads: the K4 witness therefore returns zeros on both). cudaMemset on a valid fresh allocation fails only under a sticky context error (a device fault such as an illegal address, or a lost device). No public TensorCUDA call in this round's census produces one without a memory-unsafe operation (ENG4's predicate exists to refuse those), and making the context fail on purpose on the shared GPU is outside this order (no GPU use; the lead's lines run inside GRAPA's cooldowns). Reading: matmul.cu zeros_checked (the only status branch) and kernels.cu Storage::Storage (the allocation succeeded before the fill).
m11_f3_status_ignored.run: built and run against the CPU test file (expected: every test passes, i.e. survives), and against own_F3's GPU tests only if the lead chooses; no GPU line is registered to kill it
